https://nineoclock.ro/envisia-and-henley.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount Bucharest, August 18, 2026: Envisia announces the opening of applications for the next cohort of the Henley MA Board Practice and Directorship , the international master’s programme delivered in Romania in partnership with Henley Business School – University of Reading , one of the few business schools worldwide to hold the prestigious triple accreditation (AACSB, AMBA and EQUIS). Applications are now open for all three stages of the programme: Postgraduate Certificate (Stage 1), Postgraduate Diploma (Stage 2) and Master of Arts in Board Practice and Directorship (Stage 3). Today, Envisia community includes more than 180 professional non-executive directors holding the globally recognised Henley postgraduate qualification, over 130 leaders certified in Romania, while more than 500 executives and board leaders have participated in Envisia’s executive education programmes and courses. “Over the past six years, we have seen board education in Romania move from a niche conversation to a real professional development priority for senior leaders. Together with Henley Business School, Envisia has contributed to building a community of more than 180 professionals with an internationally recognised qualification in Board Practice and Directorship. This is not only a programme milestone; it is a sign that the Romanian market is becoming more mature in how it understands governance, board responsibility and the professionalisation of the board director role” said Carmen Micu, Founder and CEO of Envisia. The Henley MA Board Practice and Directorship is an international master’s programme designed for board members and executive leaders who want to strengthen their contribution at board level. Delivered on a part-time basis over approximately two years, the programme is structured into three consecutive stages of approximately eight months each: Postgraduate Certificate (Stage 1), Postgraduate Diploma (Stage 2) and Master of Arts in Board Practice and Directorship (Stage 3). Each stage combines one intensive residential week with approximately eight months of blended learning, individual and group assessments, and applied learning activities, leading to an internationally recognised academic qualification. The curriculum covers director effectiveness, board dynamics, stewardship, investor relations, governance, innovation, risk, reputation, communication and real board-level governance challenges. It is delivered by internationally recognised Henley Business School faculty and leading experts in corporate governance, board effectiveness and leadership, including Professor Nada Kakabadse, Dr. Filipe Morais, Chris Ansell, CFA, Karen Foy, Dineshi Ramesh, Dr. Nadeem Khan and Garry Honey. Combining academic research with extensive boardroom experience, the faculty provides participants with practical insights into the governance challenges faced by boards across the private, public and third sectors. “Most directors can recall a moment when they had a doubt and did not voice it. That moment, rather than the governance code, is where boards are won or lost. This programme is for people already at the table who suspect their board could be better and want to be the one to improve it. Participants bring a live governance challenge from their own boardroom and leave having investigated it properly, with the judgement and the evidence to act on what they find ,” said Professor Nada Kakabadse, Professor of Policy, Governance and Ethics at Henley Business School . Over the years, the programme has brought together board members and senior executives from leading organisations including the Bucharest Stock Exchange, Deloitte Romania, PwC Romania, EY Romania, OMV Petrom, IBM, Raiffeisen Bank, CEC Bank, Adrem, TeraPlast, Lion Capital, Evergent Investments, Fan Curier, Regina Maria, Ursus Breweries, Energynomics, IATA, Booking.com Romania or Ana Hotels, contributing to one of Romania’s strongest executive communities dedicated to board practice and corporate governance. The Henley–Envisia partnership has also generated two volumes of Chronicles from the Boardroom , a collection of board research papers grounded in real organisational contexts across diverse industries in Romania, marking an important milestone for board practice and governance education in the local market. „In today’s volatile business landscape, boardroom leadership is no longer about intuition—it requires a refined strategic vision, ethical discipline, and the agility to navigate complex governance dilemmas. The Henley MA Board Practice and Directorship is not just an academic milestone; it is a transformative journey. By combining world-class academic rigour—backed by triple accreditation—with applied learning on live organizational challenges, we empower leaders to move from managing business to shaping sustainable futures. Joining this programme means securing your seat among an elite global network of directors who redefine board performance and drive real economic impact.” , said Dr. Gabriela Hârțescu, Dean of Envisia and Visiting Fellow, Henley Business School . The programme is designed for board members, executive and non-executive directors, independent directors, company secretaries, entrepreneurs, family business leaders and senior executives preparing for board-level governance roles. “Investors, shareholders and other stakeholders are placing increasing emphasis on the quality of corporate governance. A well-prepared board contributes to stronger decision-making, more effective risk management and greater organisational trust. Professionalising the role of the board director is an investment in the resilience and long-term competitiveness of organisations, while also supporting the development of a stronger, more transparent and more sustainable economy,” concluded Carmen Micu. Applications are now open for all three stages of the programme. Candidates entering the pathway for the first time can apply for the Postgraduate Certificate in Board Practice and Directorship — Stage 1 , while graduates of previous stages may continue their journey through the Postgraduate Diploma — Stage 2 and the Master of Arts in Board Practice and Directorship — Stage 3 . Applications for the new cohort are open until: Postgraduate Certificate (Stage 1) – 15 September 2026 Postgraduate Diploma (Stage 2) – 14 September 2026 Master of Arts in Board Practice and Directorship (Stage 3) – 9 September 2026 About Envisia Envisia is the first business school in Romania dedicated to members of boards of directors, C-suite executives and highly experienced professionals who aspire to such positions. Envisia’s mission is to create and develop, through education and specialized services, a strong community of professional board members certified to serve on boards of directors, as well as generations of leaders who embody professionalism, ethical conduct and responsibility while adding value to companies and the broader community. Envisia’s educational portfolio includes two firsts in Romania. The first is the Master of Arts in Board Practice and Directorship , the first international post-graduate academic program with triple global accreditation that professionalizes the role of a board member, delivered in partnership with Henley Business School. The second is the first post-graduate corporate governance program accredited and recognized by the Romanian Ministry of Education, “Corporate Governance that Creates Value,” launched in partnership with the Romanian-American University and the Bucharest Stock Exchange. The portfolio also includes the first professional program in Romania specifically designed for listed companies and capital market participants. In addition, Envisia offers a wide range of highly specialized short courses, delivered either in open format or customized for organizations, as well as international professional certifications on topics relevant to its target audience from public and private sector organizations across all economic sectors, including sustainable economy and ESG, banking and finance. More details are available at www.envisia.eu . About Henley Business School Henley Business School is part of the University of Reading and one of the few business schools worldwide to hold triple accreditation from AACSB, AMBA and EQUIS . With a strong international reputation in leadership, management, governance and executive education, Henley combines academic research, practical learning and global faculty expertise to support leaders and organisations across sectors. https://www.politico.eu/article/andy-bur.text: BRIGHTON, England — Zack Polanski won a landslide victory to lead the Green Party last September with a vow to “replace” Labour on the left of British politics. Today, Andy Burnham’s new-look Labour is gobbling up Polanski’s policies — and, rather than supplanting the governing Labour Party, the Greens are sliding down the polls. Burnham used a conference speech last week to frame the next general election as a fight on left-of-center, progressive issues familiar to Polanski’s brand of eco-populism — such as electoral reform, a new adult social care system, and forging closer ties with the EU. Advertisement Advertisement “Vote Green, and watch Labour move,” Polanski told his own party’s conference this past weekend, arguing that Labour’s leftward lurch on policy was down to pressure exerted via Green breakthroughs in local and parliamentary by-elections. But experts warn that it’s precisely such moves from Burnham, which the Greens chalk up as wins, that ultimately undermine the party’s electoral prospects. The Green Party is “slightly a victim of their own success,” said Luke Tryl, boss of the More in Common think tank and polling agency. Party insiders insist they still have the policies to take the fight to Labour. But Tryl compared the Greens to the UK Independence Party after 2010. The Euro-skeptic outfit under Nigel Farage had an “outsized impact on the whole of politics” — but never made substantial breakthroughs into parliament. Sinking Six months ago, Polanski had dragged the Greens to 18% with voters, a single percentage point ahead of Labour, according to POLITICO’s poll of polls , as Keir Starmer’s ruling party struggled in the doldrums. Advertisement Advertisement Now the Green Party has sunk back to 11%, and Burnham’s Labour has reopened a lead over the Greens of 14 points. The initial surge in Green support is mostly over, More in Common argued in a presentation on the fringes of the party’s annual conference, as Burnham claws back voters on the left. Zack Polanski participates in a protest in London on Nov. 25, 2025. | Guy Smallman/Getty Images John Curtice, Britain’s leading political scientist, compared the party’s fortunes to another force in British politics. “This reminds me of the kind of arguments that the Liberal Democrats used to use,” he said: “‘We are the party that comes up with all the clever ideas first, and other people gobble them up.’” He added: “I think the challenge they [the Greens] now face is how do they hang on to — or in a sense recapture — the support that they did have six months ago, that seems to have eroded back to Labour.” To the left, to the left Burnham’s speech to Labour conference last Tuesday — which the party faithful met with tears and applause — indicates the size of that challenge. Burnham proposed a state-funded social care system in the mold of the NHS, as well as promising electoral reform and a new long-term relationship between Britain and the EU. (He later left the door open to another referendum.) “They are all policies that we already have,” Sian Berry, Green MP for Brighton Pavilion, answered when POLITICO reeled through Burnham’s priorities. “It is hard to imagine that speech ... without the influence of the Green Party,” Tryl said. Advertisement Advertisement The principle of a care system free at the point of need, for example, “has been in Green Party policy for some years now,” said Adrian Ramsay, MP for Waveney Valley. The party also backs “closer ties” with the EU post-Brexit and, eventually, rejoining the bloc . On electoral reform, the Greens are left agreeing with Labour but urging Burnham to move faster. A commission, tasked with suggesting how to shake up the electoral system before the next election, could “just be the way to kick this into the long grass,” said Natalie Bennett, a Green Party peer. “What we are saying is PR [proportional representation] now.” Being distinctive Green Party politicians are keen to talk up areas where they still offer voters something distinct from Labour. Polanski’s main policy announcement in his speech was a temporary “emergency brake” on private rent, which would stop rents rising above 2%, inflation, or levels of wage growth, whichever was lowest. Burnham, when mayor of Manchester, voiced support for rent controls — only for his government to rule it out this summer . John Curtice said those plans could help shore up the Green vote. “Polanski’s policy on rent is very, very clearly designed to appeal to precisely the kind of people that Greens have been most successful among,” he said. “We’re not afraid to say that there should be more regulation on landlords,” said Zoë Garbett, the Green mayor of Hackney, who won her seat from Labour in May’s local elections. Advertisement Advertisement Green members also passed a policy motion ditching the Office for Budget Responsibility and scrapping fiscal rules seen to constrain public spending. The party has drawn dividing lines with the government, too, on climate, its founding cause. Alongside Gaza, it was Polanski’s call to ban new oil and gas drilling in the North Sea that received the loudest applause in the hall. A pro-Palestine demonstration takes place during the Green Party conference in Brighton, England on Oct. 3, 2026. | Alishia Abodunde/Getty Images “The Andy Burnham speech was impressive in its oratory, and it was clearly a shift from what we saw from Keir Starmer, but there wasn’t a single mention of climate and nature in the whole speech,” Ramsay said. The same More in Common data referenced above showed that Green voters, and those considering voting for the Greens, think the party is at its best when talking about nature and clean power. Rethinking climate goals And yet, the Green’s Brighton conference also saw the party waver on its ambitious, flagship climate pledge. The Greens went into the 2024 general election with a promise to reduce U.K. greenhouse gas emissions to net zero by 2040 , a full decade ahead of Labour’s target. Advertisement Advertisement But that bold commitment has gone. “We would need to review [the pledge],” said Ramsay, when asked if the net-zero target still stood. “We did a really thorough exercise ahead of the 2024 manifesto to look at what’s the quickest it can be achieved from that point in time. We will do the same ahead of the next general election.” He blamed slow progress on net zero by “repeated governments.” Meantime, said Curtice, the political scientist, the Greens should focus on offering answers to short-term challenges on issues like cost of living and turning around the health service. Hannah Spencer — the MP for Gorton and Denton, who beat Labour in a by-election earlier this year — last week accused the government of “dithering” over intervening with support for energy bills, which are expected to surge in January. There is always a chance for the Greens in “profiting from disillusion with Labour,” argued Curtice. The party’s task, he added, is to come up at the same time with policies that “encourage people.” Hannah Brenton contributed additional reporting.
